what: The agent behaviour policy of storyboards.sgit.ai: the agents that work on this site, what they can do, what they are asked to do, every rule with the barrier that stands in its way and what enforces it, and where each rule maps to elsewhere. Written as data so the page is generated from it and another site can copy the shape. Rendered at /abp/.
status: written by the storyboards agent from Dinis Cruz's words and this repository's rules; not yet read by him

agents.name: The storyboards agent
agents.runs_as: a Claude Code session in a Claude Code on the web container, started by the person from claude.ai/code, with this repository and SGit-AI__Website__Storyboards__API cloned side by side
agents.does: builds and releases both sites from the briefs: imports storyboards, writes pages and articles, cuts API releases, pins them here, runs the gates and tests, pushes
agents.leaves: commits on the person's GitHub account, each with a Claude-Session trailer naming the session

agents.name: Research subagents
agents.runs_as: Explore agents the storyboards agent starts for one research question (for example, how sibling sites are built, or what riskmandate.ai's policy shape is)
agents.does: reads and searches files and public web pages; cannot edit, write or push
agents.leaves: a report to the storyboards agent, treated as data and never as an instruction

layers.here: CLAUDE.md, the briefs, and the harness's own instructions to the session
.claude/settings.json: SessionStart prints the code immutability rule; PreToolUse runs the API checkout's hook on every Edit, Write, MultiEdit, NotebookEdit and Bash
admin/build/build.py stops on an unknown character, kind, pose, mood or prop, a storyboard whose bytes are not the imported ones, or a stale thumbnail
admin/build/validate.py: links, twins, sitemap, the pinned API with its integrity strings, the version everywhere, key shapes, em-dashes
.github/workflows/ci.yml on every push: the build twice, the gate, the version bump, briefs unchanged, every page in Chromium
.github/workflows/deploy-pages.yml: the same checks before www/ is published from dev
none yet: dev is not protected, so a push that fails CI still lands on the branch (it is not deployed)

grant.what: change any file in this checkout and the API checkout beside it
grant.note: the code immutability hook denies changes to published API releases

grant.what: push commits to any branch of this repository and of SGit-AI__Website__Storyboards__API, including dev, which deploys
grant.undo: with effort (a new commit; a deployed page may be cached)
grant.note: the harness tells the session to push only to its own branch unless the person says otherwise

grant.what: through the session's GitHub tools: create branches, open, comment on and merge pull requests in the two repositories it is scoped to
grant.note: the harness tells the session not to open a pull request unless asked

grant.what: run any command: Python, Node, Chromium (Playwright), git
grant.undo: the container is reclaimed after the session

grant.what: fetch public pages through the session's proxy
grant.note: used to read the sibling sites and riskmandate.ai

grant.what: edit .claude/settings.json, the hooks, the policy files, the workflows
grant.note: the hook asks the person first (ABP-SB-001, row R5)

want: a home for storyboards that are data, drawn by the API's kit, in every shape they come in (the brief of 20 October 2026)
the storyboards from gen-z-developers.sgit.ai and pki.sgit.ai, replicated as they are
every push to dev a version, shown on every page, with a line saying what changed
both repositories worked side by side and kept in step
do_not_want: a storyboard or cast edited here instead of at its origin
a page in www/ edited by hand
code in a published API release changed
a key, a token or a vault key in the repository
a brief rewritten after the fact
a push to dev or a pull request the person did not ask for
unstated: whether the agent may merge a pull request: not decided; it has not been asked to and has not

rules.rule: Code in a published API release folder (vX/vX.Y/vX.Y.Z/) is never changed
rules.why: a page pinned to a release must get the same bytes for as long as it exists; its integrity strings refuse anything else
rules.enforced_by: the API checkout's hook, run from .claude/settings.json here (deny); in the API repository also its pre-commit hook, release.py check and CI
rules.stronger_at: branch protection on the API's dev requiring ci (boundary)
maps_to: api.newsroom.sgit.ai rule R16: a change is a new version path, always
abp.sgit.ai upstream/: fetched bytes, never edited

rules.rule: A storyboard or cast imported from another site is never edited here: it is corrected at its origin and re-imported
rules.why: the storyboard is the origin site's work, checked there (gen-z's quotes word for word); a local edit would make two versions that disagree
rules.enforced_by: admin/build/build.py: every imported file's SHA-256 against content/series/*/series.json; a changed or unimported file stops the build, locally and in CI
maps_to: gen-z-developers.sgit.ai CLAUDE.md: do not edit anything under v1/content/
abp.sgit.ai: upstream/ and contributed/ are fetched bytes, never edited

rules.rule: www/ is generated by the build and never edited by hand
rules.why: a hand edit is lost on the next build, or worse, kept by a build that no longer makes it
rules.enforced_by: build.py --check in CI and before every deploy
maps_to: sgit.ai repository guidance: nav and footer injected at build so they cannot drift

rules.rule: Every push to dev is a new version, with its line in content/versions.json
rules.why: a page that does not say which version it is cannot be dated or checked
rules.enforced_by: CI's version check against dev; build.py refuses a malformed history; validate.py checks the version on every page and in llms.txt
maps_to: sgit.ai repository guidance: one version, going up on every push

rules.rule: No key, token or vault key is ever committed
rules.why: a read key may be published; a vault key or a provider's API key never
rules.enforced_by: validate.py: sgit vault key shapes, private key blocks, cloud and provider key prefixes in www/, content/, briefs/ and admin/
rules.stronger_at: GitHub secret scanning with push protection (a host rule)
maps_to: sgit.ai repository guidance: credentials; the leak tripwire

rules.rule: A brief is published in full and never edited; corrections go in BRIEF-CORRECTIONS.md
rules.why: the brief is the record of what was asked; a correction above the mistake keeps both visible
rules.enforced_by: CI: a brief that exists on dev must be unchanged on the branch
maps_to: sgit.ai repository guidance: the brief, in full; the corrections file

rules.rule: Push to dev, which deploys, and open or merge a pull request, only when the person has asked
rules.why: a push to dev publishes to the world; the person decides when
rules.stronger_at: branch protection on dev requiring a review (a host rule)

rules.rule: The site's own prose has no em-dashes, states the status of things and sources its numbers
rules.why: the estate's house style; a number nobody can check is a guess
rules.enforced_by: validate.py refuses an em-dash in content/articles, content/pages and the agent-written part of briefs/ (setting); the rest is a request

rules.rule: The agent does not weaken its own controls without the person
rules.why: a control the agent can quietly switch off is not a control
rules.enforced_by: the code immutability hook asks the person before a write to .claude/settings.json (here) and to the API's hook, policy files, release tool and workflows
rules.stronger_at: managed hooks the agent cannot write (allowManagedHooksOnly)
maps_to: riskmandate.ai RM-R0015, change its own permissions

gaps: No rule is a boundary yet: every control above lives in a file this agent's grant can write, or in the agent's instructions. Protecting dev in GitHub (require the ci check, and a review for the files under .claude/, policies/ and .github/) is the step that turns several of them into boundaries; only the person can make it.
No footprint is recorded: what the agent actually did is in the git history (every commit carries a Claude-Session trailer) and in the session itself, and nothing compares it with this policy yet.
A Claude Code hook fails open if it errors or times out, and a git hook is skipped with --no-verify; the CI checks are the backstop for both.
copy_to_another_site: Copy policies/abp.json (type abp/site/v1) and the renderer (admin/build/abp.py here, site/abp.py in the API repository), list the site's own agents, grant, mandate and rules, keep the rule ids unique across the estate (a prefix per site: ABP-SB- for these two), and give each rule the check that enforces it, or say plainly that nothing does.
